rulings.Case Title: IN RE: THE GEORGE HERBST 2009 TRUST,DATED APRIL 9, 2009
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Demurrer And Demurrer To Petitioner'S Complaint
rulings.Rulings: This tentative ruling is issued by Judge Russell S. Roeca. Before the court is Respondent John P. Hurabeill's Demurrer to Petitioner's Complaint ("Demurrer"). The Demurrer is set to be heard concurrently with Respondent John P. Hurabeill's Motion to Strike Petitioners' Prayer for Punitive Damages in the Petition. Per the Notice of Demurrer, Respondent demurrers to the First and Third causes of action pursuant to Code of Civil Procedure sections 430.10(e) and (f), for failure to state a cause of action. Before filing a demurrer, moving party's counsel must meet and confer either in person, by video conference, or by telephone with petitioner's counsel in an attempt to reach an informal agreement that would resolve the objections. It appears the meet and confer efforts over this Demurrer, filed in this court, were all over email, which is not in compliance with the relevant Code. Counsel for all parties are reminded to comply with the relevant statutes, reasonably and in good faith, before seeking the court's intervention. When considering a demurrer, the trial court must accept as true all material facts pleaded in the complaint and those arising by reasonable implication. (Moore v. Conliffe (1994) 7 Cal.4th 634, 638; Montclair Parkowners Ass'n v. City of Montclair (1999) 76 Cal. App. 4th 784.) This does not apply to allegations expressing mere conclusions of law. (Vance v. Villa Park Mobilehome Estates (1995) 36 Cal. App. 4th 698, 709.) The Demurrer to the First and Third causes of action as to Hurabeill, pursuant to Code of Civil Procedure sections 430.10(f), is OVERRULED. The papers made no showing as to the Petition's "uncertainty," ambiguity or unintelligibility. The Demurrer to the First and Third causes of action as to Hurabeill, pursuant to Code of Civil Procedure sections 430.10(e), is SUSTAINED with leave to amend. The First cause of action seeks to invalidate the contested trust amendment on the basis of undue influence. While the Petition facially alleges the elements of undue influence over Decedent by Respondent Barnett's, the Petition does not allege facts, facially or arising by reasonable implication, that Hurabeill committed the elements of undue influence over Decedent. The Third cause of action is for Financial Elder Abuse. The Petition alleges, on information and belief, Hurebeill committed financial elder abuse as defined in Welf. & Inst. Code sec. 15610.30 by aiding Respondent Barnett in her wrongful conduct, specifically by drafting the challenged estate planning documents when he "knew or should have known" the documents were being procured by undue influence and/or financial elder abuse. Demurrer is sustained with leave to amend to allow Petitioners opportunity to allege the source(s) of that information and belief. An amended petition shall be filed within 10 days of entry of this Order. Any party wishing to contest this tentative ruling by appearing at the scheduled hearing must so advise other parties and the courtroom clerk (415-551-3702) no later than 4:00 p.m. on the day before the hearing. To appear by Zoom, go to zoom.us and click "Join Meeting." Enter Meeting ID number 1602254765 and passcode 514879. To appear telephonically through Zoom, call 1-669-900-6833 and follow the prompts. Enter Meeting ID number 1602254765# and passcode 514879#. Parties appearing via Zoom should use their full names in the "Your Name" section. rulings.Case Title: IN RE: THE GEORGE HERBST 2009 TRUST,DATED APRIL 9, 2009
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion To Strike Petitioners' Prayer For Punitive Damages In The Petition
rulings.Rulings: [Part 1 of 2] This tentative ruling is issued by Judge Russell S. Roeca. Before the court is Respondent John P. Hurabeill's Motion to Strike Petitioners' Prayer for Punitive Damages in the Petition ("Motion"). The Motion is set to be heard concurrently with Respondent John P. Hurabeill's Demurrer to the Petition. The Motion is GRANTED, with leave to amend, as follows. Before filing a motion to strike, moving party's counsel must meet and confer either in person, by video conference, or by telephone with petitioner's counsel in an attempt to reach an informal agreement that would resolve the objections to the pleading and obviate the need for filing a motion to strike. (Code of Civil Procedure secs. 435.5, 2016.040.) It appears from counsel's declaration in support of the Motion that after the Petition was filed in this court the parties' attorneys communicated over email to attempt informal resolution of the issues now presented by the Motion. Email communication does not comply with the statutory requirements to meet either person, by video conference, or by telephone. Counsel for all parties are reminded to comply with the relevant statutes, reasonably and in good faith, before seeking the court's intervention. Respondent moves to strike the Petition's prayer for punitive damages sought under Civil Code sec. 3294, on grounds that the Petition does not plead sufficient facts to support the punitive damages request and it is thus "improper matter" pursuant to Code of Civil Procedure section 436. Here, the Petition's prayer for relief, at paragraph 14, seeks "[P]unitive damages and exemplary damages under California Civil Code Section 3294 and California Welfare & Institutions Code Section 15657.5 according to proof." Under Civil Code Section 3294(a), "In an action for the breach of an obligation not arising from contract, where it is proven by clear and convincing evidence that the defendant has been guilty of oppression, fraud, or malice, the plaintiff, in addition to the actual damages, may recover damages for the sake of example and by way of punishing the defendant." The statute defines those terms in subsection (c): "Malice" means conduct which is intended by the defendant to cause injury to the plaintiff or despicable conduct which is carried on by the defendant with a willful and conscious disregard of the rights or safety of others. "Oppression" means despicable conduct that subjects a person to cruel and unjust hardship in conscious disregard of that person's rights. "Fraud" means an intentional misrepresentation, deceit, or concealment of a material fact known to the defendant with the intention on the part of the defendant of thereby depriving a person of property or legal rights or otherwise causing injury. In ruling on a motion to strike, the Petition's allegations are read in their context and presumed to be true. (See, Clauson v. Sup.Ct. (Pedus Services, Inc.) (1998) 67 CA4th 1253, 1255.) The Petition at paragraphs 23, 47, 48, 49, 50, 52 alleges, in summary, that Respondent Hurabiell knowingly assisted the other Responent, Barnett, by drafting the contested trust instrument despite knowing of Decedent's vulnerability and prior estate planning and his own conflict of interest as Decedent's drafting attorney due to his friendship with Barnett, and thereby "denied [Decedent] the right to have his assets distributed according to his true testementary intent[.]" (Par. 50.) Petitioner, in the Opposition to the Motion, argues these allegations "support a reasonable inference that Respondent acted with malive, oppression, or fraud within the meaning of Civil Code section 3294," because the Petition alleges Respondent knowlingly participated in transcations procured by undue influence and affecting Decedent's propety rights (Opp. at 4:7-8, 15-17.)

rulings.Rulings: [Part 2 of 2] A motion to strike may lie where the facts alleged do not rise to the level of "malice, fraud or oppression" required to support a punitive damages award. (See, Turman v. Turning Point of Central Calif., Inc. (2010) 191 CA4th 53, 63.) The Petition does not, on its face, allege facts showing "conduct which is intended by the defendant to cause injury to the plaintiff," or "despicable conduct which is carried on by the defendant with a willful and conscious disregard of the rights or safety of others" or "despicable conduct that subjects a person to cruel and unjust hardship in conscious disregard of that person's rights" or "intentional misrepresentation, deceit, or concealment of a material fact known to the defendant with the intention on the part of the defendant of thereby depriving a person of property or legal rights or otherwise causing injury." The request for relief under Civil Code sec. 3294 is not supported by the allegations, and is thus "irrelevant matter" and subject to a motion to strike (see, Code of Civil Procedure secs. 431.10, 436). An amended Petition shall be filed within 10 days of entry of this Order.
